introStyles: problem-led: Open with the specific problem the business owner is facing — describe it vividly. Then show the impact on their business before introducing the solution.
outcome-led: Open with the positive result the business could have — a concrete picture of what changes when they get this right. Then show the gap between where they are now and that outcome.
trust-led: Open by establishing the landscape — who is succeeding locally and why. Position the reader as someone who already understands quality, then introduce the service as the natural next step.

local-competition-led: Open by naming the competitive reality of this specific area — how many similar businesses are online and what separates the ones winning enquiries. Then position the service as the lever that changes that.
ctaStyles: quote-focused: Drive toward a specific quote or proposal. Make it easy and low-commitment — just a brief description of what they need.
consultation-focused: Offer a short discovery conversation. Position it as a chance to get clarity, not a sales pitch.
low-pressure: Remove all pressure — no obligation, no hard sell. Emphasise that the first step is just a quick conversation or message.
growth-focused: Connect the CTA to the business outcome they want — more enquiries, more visibility, more growth. Make taking action feel like a business decision, not a purchase.
